冶 concerns smelting and working metals. Learn it through 冶金 (やきん), metallurgy: the science and technology of obtaining and working metals. Not every use is literal metalworking: 陶冶 (とうや) can mean cultivation or training, for example of character or abilities.

Modern-shape mnemonic: imagine the two cold 冫 marks beside a 台-shaped work stand where metal is being shaped. This is an invented memory aid, not a historical derivation or a verified explanation of the sound.
Both source readings remain below. Only ヤ is selected for reading practice.

Compare 治, "govern; heal": its left side has three water strokes, 氵, rather than 冶's two strokes, 冫. 始, "begin," has 女 on the left. Sharing the 台-shaped right side does not make these characters interchangeable.

鍛冶 (かじ), "blacksmithing; blacksmith," has a special whole-word reading. Do not extract ジ from its final kana and add it to 冶's on readings. The dictionaries also document the separate reading たんや for 鍛冶.
For general melting or dissolving, compare 溶 and 溶かす (とかす). 冶 is not the ordinary spelling to substitute into a sentence about melting butter or dissolving sugar.

冶金 やきん — metallurgy

冶金 is metallurgy: the science and technology of extracting metals from raw materials and working them into useful materials and forms. It includes more than simply melting something. It is a technical noun.
大学で冶金を学んでいます。 (だいがくでやきんをまなんでいます。) — I am studying metallurgy at university.
冶金について研究しています。 (やきんについてけんきゅうしています。) — I am doing research on metallurgy.
冶金を学ぶ (やきんをまなぶ) means "study metallurgy"; 冶金について (やきんについて) means "about metallurgy."

冶 (ヤ) contributes smelting or working metal. 金 (キン) means metal here, not money or gold alone. The relationship is action plus object: working metal. The whole noun names the technical field, not just one operation. This is a meaning aid, not an account of the word's historical formation.

冶金学 (やきんがく) specifically names metallurgy as a science. 金属 (きんぞく) means the material "metal," not the field that studies and processes it. 製錬 and 精錬 (both せいれん) concern smelting or refining: related processes rather than the whole discipline. There is no useful everyday opposite of the field's name.

冶金 belongs in scientific, educational and industrial contexts. It does not mean making money, and it is not limited to gold. 錬金術 (れんきんじゅつ), "alchemy," is a different term, not a synonym for modern metallurgy.
Use 溶かす (とかす) when describing an action such as melting butter or dissolving sugar; 冶金 names the metalworking field and its technology, not any act of making something liquid.
